name: Shaukat Ali
contribution: Alongside his brother Mohammad Ali Jauhar and other leaders, he helped initiate and organize the Khilafat movement and connect it to Gandhi’s Non-Cooperation campaign.
context: The Ali brothers mobilized Indian Muslim opinion in defence of the Ottoman Caliphate after World War I, while also building a wider anti-colonial alliance with Congress leaders. Shaukat Ali’s activism included public campaigning, political organization, and imprisonment by the colonial government.
impact: He helped turn the Khilafat question into a mass political campaign and made Muslim leadership central to the Non-Cooperation moment. His career also shows how that alliance weakened after the movement’s suspension and the abolition of the Ottoman Caliphate.
highlight: Ali Brothers leader who connected Khilafat mobilization with Non-Cooperation politics.
seoTitle: Shaukat Ali: Khilafat Leader and Anti-Colonial Organizer
seoDescription: Learn about Shaukat Ali, the Ali Brothers leader who organized the Khilafat movement and linked it with Gandhi’s Non-Cooperation campaign.
shortAnswer: Shaukat Ali was a principal Khilafat leader who worked with Mohammad Ali Jauhar and Gandhi’s Congress alliance during the Non-Cooperation movement.

faq.question: What was Shaukat Ali’s role in the Khilafat movement?
faq.answer: He was one of its principal organizers, working with Mohammad Ali Jauhar, Abul Kalam Azad, and other leaders to mobilize Indian Muslims.

faq.question: How was Shaukat Ali connected to Non-Cooperation?
faq.answer: The Khilafat leadership, including Shaukat Ali, supported Gandhi’s Non-Cooperation campaign and helped turn it into a broader anti-colonial mass movement.
